AI Identifies Clinically Relevant Asystole Among False Loop Recorder Alerts: From Data Overload to Diagnosis.
desc: [JACC. Case reports] Implantable loop recorders (ILRs) are often implanted to investigate unexplained syncopal episodes. However, ILRs may produce false alerts due to undersensing or artifacts, thus requiring careful review of numerous device recordings, which makes it challenging to identify clinically significant events. We report a case of a 77-year-old woman with recurrent syncopal episodes, in whom a 7-second pause was detected by an ILR. Device interrogations showed multiple pause alerts that were identified as false events because of poor R sensing. However, the artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced remote monitoring identified a true pause with blocked P waves, leading the patient to receive a pacemaker implantation. This case highlights the clinical value of AI-assisted remote monitoring in identifying clinically relevant arrhythmias among numerous device alerts. Improved automated filtering of ILR data may reduce diagnostic delays and help clinicians prioritize clinically significant events. ILRs may generate numerous false alerts because of sensing abnormalities, complicating the identification of clinically relevant events in routine practice. AI-enhanced remote monitoring may improve diagnostic efficiency by identifying true arrhythmic events within large volumes of device-generated data and guiding timely management.

title: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Facial Phenotyping and Diagnosis of Rare Genetic Disorders
desc: Rare genetic disorders are difficult to diagnose due to their diversity and overlapping clinical features. Facial morphology can provide diagnostic clues, yet most diagnostic models offer limited interpretability and are not designed to support broad screening for undiagnosed disease. We present ProtoGestalt, an interpretable prototype-based framework for facial phenotyping, rare-disease screening, and syndrome identification. The method extends prototype learning by constraining learned visual features to select facial regions, allowing predictions to be explained through localized and additive evidence. We assess ProtoGestalt's ability to distinguish syndromic from unaffected faces on multiple control datasets and class prevalence values. We further evaluate it's diagnostic performance on syndromes observed during training. The learned prototype-based representations provide significant separation between syndromic and case-matched control images and retain useful performance as the proportion of controls increases. The framework also demonstrates the ability to differentiate among syndromes. Although reasonably accurate specialized models for facial classification of rare disorders already exist, ProtoGestalt offers an interpretable alternative that links predictions to anatomically meaningful facial regions, potentially supporting clinical decision-making and the discovery of phenotype-gene associations.

title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction.
desc: [Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)] The rise of Alzheimer's disease (AD) immunotherapies underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. MRI-based deep learning shows promise in this regard, yet few models have undergone comprehensive clinical validation. Using the SILCODE cohort (722 Chinese participants, 1,105 scans), we test the transportability of our classifier (pretrained on Western samples) to an independent Chinese cohort without retraining. The associations between risk scores and disease progression, cognitive performance, and plasma biomarkers are examined. In addition, an interpretable framework is developed to generate individualized brain risk maps and identify subtypes. The model classifies AD with an AUC of 0.913 and 95.2% sensitivity, identifying 90.5% of high-risk individuals 2-3 years before clinical diagnosis. Risk scores correlate significantly with cognitive and plasma indices, particularly p-tau 217. Brain risk maps reveal AD subtypes, including a subgroup with rapid cognitive decline. These findings establish a population-robust, clinically relevant MRI-based model for early AD detection and risk stratification.

title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image
desc: In healthcare, protecting patient privacy is crucial due to the sensitivity of medical data and its extensive accessibility. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving training paradigm, making it an ideal solution for healthcare applications. A critical challenge in healthcare is that real-world medical data often exhibits long-tailed distributions in local and global views. Existing methods addressing long-tailed FL problem typically assume that the model will be evaluated on uniform test data distribution. However, practical test data in healthcare systems is often agnostic and unpredictable, leading to potential model failures in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a novel task termed Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning and propose GTAFL, a comprehensive framework to address this challenge. During the training stage, GTAFL employs adaptive re-sampling, expert classifier retraining, and self-supervised learning to correct biased classifiers and distorted feature spaces caused by long-tailed training distributions. During the inference stage, an ensemble mechanism combines retrained expert classifiers to handle test data with unknown distributions. Extensive experiments on CIFAR10 and two medical datasets manifest that our framework outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/cgy-lavine/GTAFL

title: MultiMHC: a multiscale learning framework integrating sequence and residue contact topology for peptide-MHC binding prediction.
desc: [Briefings in bioinformatics] Accurate prediction of peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) binding is central to understanding antigen presentation and identifying T-cell epitopes in cancer immunotherapy. Although recent methods have achieved notable progress, most approaches rely predominantly on sequence-based features and only partially capture structural determinants of pMHC recognition. In this study, we present MultiMHC, a multiscale deep learning framework that integrates complementary sequential and biologically-informed residue contact topology for pMHC binding prediction. MultiMHC combines a recurrent neural network to model global sequence context with a graph-based representation to encode residue contact patterns derived from known pMHC binding interfaces. Features from these two pathways are subsequently fused to generate binding predictions across peptides of varying lengths. Benchmark evaluations show that MultiMHC achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art methods, with particularly strong performance in ranking-based assessments. Moreover, evaluation on the Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance dataset showed that MultiMHC binding scores can enrich experimentally validated T-cell epitopes among top-ranked candidates, supporting its potential utility as an upstream binding-based filtering step in neoantigen discovery workflows. Together, these results highlight the value of incorporating residue interaction patterns and lightweight structural information into pMHC modeling and establish MultiMHC as a robust and extensive framework for antigen presentation analysis.

title: Synthesis of Ovarian Cancer Multi-Omics Datasets: A Biology-Informed Evaluation Framework
desc: Paired multi-omic cancer cohorts are costly to assemble and difficult to share, motivating synthetic cohorts as a complementary resource. As generative model development accelerates, we shift the focus from proposing yet another architecture to defining evaluation criteria that determine whether synthetic data preserve biologically relevant structure. We introduce a biology-informed and patient-disjoint framework for evaluating the generation of paired RNA expression and copy-number variation (CNV) profiles, and apply it to the longitudinal DECIDER high-grade serous ovarian cancer cohort. The framework assesses modality-specific fidelity and coherence between RNA and CNV pairs using agreement between real training and held-out data as a reference, alongside complementary training-data proximity diagnostics. We adapt three multi-omic integration architectures based on variational autoencoders to generate paired profiles. The model leading several fidelity and coherence measures also shows the strongest training-data proximity. The protocol and case study offer the community a reference for comparing future multi-omic generators.

title: ToxPipe: integrating AI into toxicoinformatics.
desc: [Frontiers in toxicology] ToxPipe is a modular, fully open-source software stack designed to accelerate toxicological data analysis and decision-making by integrating large language model (LLM) capabilities with workflow, monitoring, and user-interface services. ToxPipe leverages existing open-source technologies like LibreChat, LiteLLM, and Langflow to provide centralized and streamlined access to different LLMs for end users and developers and logging and auditing of LLM use for organizations. ToxPipe also allows for open-source/local model support. While the ToxPipe ecosystem also supports advanced AI functions such as MCP server integration, RAG and literature search, and agent creation, we did not observe clear benefits using these configurations relative to the GPT-5.5 baseline assertion coverage scores. ToxPipe is available as a series of Docker containers for rapid and reproducible deployment.

title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
desc: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.

title: SECNet: Differentiable Mask-Driven Spatiotemporal Learning for Video-Based Spontaneous Echo Contrast Severity Detection.
source: PubMed · IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
desc: [IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics] Spontaneous Echo Contrast (SEC), characterized by smoke-like dynamic echogenicity in trans esophageal echocardiography (TEE), serves as a critical imaging biomarker for assessing thromboembolic risk. However, current diagnostic approaches depend on manual interpretation or regression-based algorithms, which are labor-intensive, prone to inconsistency, and limited in generalizability. To address these challenges, we propose SECNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework for auto mated SEC detection in TEE videos. SECNet incorporates two key components: (1) a region-of-interest segmentation module that accurately localizes SEC-prone cardiac structures while suppressing surrounding noise; and (2) a spa tiotemporal feature extraction module that captures both temporal dynamics and spatial distribution of SEC. These modules are linked through a novel differentiable mask guided bridging mechanism that enables joint optimization of localization and representation learning. Trained on a clinical dataset of 1,106 annotated TEE videos, SECNet achieves 93.7% accuracy and a 90.0% F1-score, outper forming the compared methods by 3.1-23.3 percentage points in accuracy. An auxiliary experiment on EchoNet Dynamic further demonstrates the applicability of the architecture to a related echocardiographic video-analysis task. This study supports standardized and reproducible SEC assessment to assist thromboembolic risk evaluation in clinical workflows.

title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
desc: [British journal of neurosurgery] Artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical prediction are proliferating across neurosurgery, but their aggregate discriminative performance, distribution along the care pathway and methodological quality are unclear. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed these studies in neurosurgery and its subspecialities along with their risk of bias appraisal. We performed a PRISMA search on PubMed and Ovid for peer-reviewed original studies (2015-2026) using AI to predict a clinical outcome in neurosurgical populations. Metrics (primary- AUC; secondary- accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, c-index) were pooled using random effects modelling, overall, by subspeciality and care-pathway stage. Each study was classified as diagnostic, prognostic or forecasting and was assigned an evidence level. Clinical prediction task sub-stratification analysis was performed. Risk-of-bias was assessed using PROBAST. PROSPERO registered: CRD420261436614. 1063 studies were included. Across 451 (42.2%) studies reporting AUC, pooled discrimination was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.849-0.862), ranging from 0.84 (spine) to 0.87 (neuro-oncology), with extreme heterogeneity (I2 98.6%, τ2=0.27; 95% prediction interval: 0.68-0.94). Performance varied by clinical pathway stage, highest for diagnosis, grading and molecular tasks and lowest for post-operative tasks; pre-diagnosis, pre-operative and intra-operative applications were sparse, and treatment models were confined to neuro-oncology. Only 51 studies (4.8%) were using prospective data with external validation, whereas 619 (58%) rested on internal validation alone or no validation. 89% studies were at high risk-of-bias, driven by the analysis domain. Pooled discrimination was unchanged (AUC: 0.86%) when restricted to externally validated or non-high-risk studies. AI models report high performance across all the neurosurgical subspecialities, concordant across AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity and robust to risk-of-bias stratification. Performance is highest for imaging-anchored diagnostic tasks and lowest at decision-facing post-operative stage. However, the literature is dominated by optimism-prone, internally-validated and poorly calibrated models with extreme heterogeneity. External validation, calibration analysis and reporting guidelines adherence remain prerequisites for clinical adoption.

title: A Deep Learning-Driven Approach for Musical Instrument Sound Synthesis and Acoustic Optimization.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] This structured narrative review examines deep‑learning‑driven musical instrument timbre synthesis, covering playing‑condition control, acoustic defect diagnosis, structural inverse design, and subjective‑objective quality evaluation. Adopting a structured narrative review method, this work follows the main themes of technical paradigms, application closed loops, supporting resources, evaluation evidence, and industrial constraints. Relevant methods are organized as direct fitting of waveforms or spectrograms to hybrid modeling embedded with physical priors, and further toward interpretable end‑to‑end systems built upon differentiable digital signal processing (DDSP) and differentiable physical modeling. A closed‑loop research framework of "multimodal evidence‑physical constraint‑perceptual evaluation‑human‑in‑the‑loop" is proposed in this paper. The major findings are as follows: pure data‑driven models possess strong representation capability yet suffer from data bias and uncontrolled extrapolation; physical priors can boost sample efficiency and parameter interpretability, whereas their benefits depend on the accuracy of priors and optimization stability; differentiable acoustics provides a unified interface for synthesis, inversion, and design, but still encounters challenges including high‑frequency gradient pathology, multi‑physics coupling, real‑time computation and incomplete perceptual objectives. Future research directions include cross‑cultural musical‑instrument datasets, digital twins with uncertainty estimation, auditable auditory preference models, low‑latency edge‑end deployment, and governance of copyright and performer rights. This study provides a unified conceptual framework and reusable evaluation pathways for music‑acoustics researchers, algorithm developers, and lutherie engineers.

title: FieldMaizeLeaf-8: A real-field early vegetative maize leaf stress image dataset from Bangladesh.
desc: [Data in brief] Maize (Zea mays L.) is a rapidly expanding cereal crop in Bangladesh, but its yield is threatened by biotic diseases, insect pests, and nutrient-deficiency disorders that are difficult to distinguish visually, particularly at the early vegetative stage. Most publicly available leaf-image datasets used to train computer-vision models for crop diagnosis are captured under controlled laboratory conditions with plain backgrounds, which limits the field-readiness of models trained on them. FieldMaizeLeaf-8 addresses this gap by providing 3975 RGB photographs of maize leaves aged approximately 1-2 months, captured directly in commercial maize fields in Daudkandi, Cumilla, Bangladesh, using a consumer smartphone under natural daylight, background, and viewing-angle conditions, with no laboratory staging. Images are organised into eight classes: one healthy-leaf class and seven stress classes, comprising three biotic conditions (Fall Armyworm damage, Leaf Spot, and Northern Corn Leaf Blight) and four abiotic nutrient-deficiency conditions (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, and Magnesium deficiency). Class labels assigned in the field were subsequently reviewed and validated by a plant-pathology expert. The dataset retains natural variability in illumination, leaf orientation, and symptom severity, and is intended to serve as a real-field benchmark for developing and evaluating deep-learning models for maize stress recognition, transfer learning, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) applications in precision agriculture.

title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
desc: [iScience] Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with static microenvironment analysis to identify enzyme variants compatible with biomimetic cofactors. Applied to P450BM3, a widely used biocatalyst for chiral synthesis and pharmaceutical precursor production, HelixWings identified a variant with a 404% improvement in catalytic efficiency toward cytochrome c under NMNH-supported conditions. The platform was further validated with CYP116B46, achieving a 217% improvement in NMNH utilization efficiency. HelixWings reduced screening time by 23-fold compared with rational design.

title: kinGEMs: A robust and scalable framework for resource-constraint models through stochastic tuning of deep learning-predicted kinetic parameters.
desc: [PLoS computational biology] The construction of accurate enzyme-constrained genome-scale models (ecGEMs) remains a critical challenge in systems biology, limited by sparse kinetic data and the need for biologically meaningful representations. This work presents an integrated framework combining CPI-Pred, a deep learning model to predict kinetic parameters (kcat) from sequence and compound embeddings, with kinGEMs, a pipeline to incorporate these uncertainty-aware parameters into ecGEMs for metabolic optimization. By leveraging representations at multiple scales, the approach captures sequence, structure, and kinetic data to enhance model generalizability and accuracy. Rigorous benchmarking demonstrates the framework's capability to predict growth rates and fluxes that are consistent with experimental observations and measured proteome fractions, reduce median flux variability by several folds, and yield better-constrained metabolic models by explicitly accounting for the uncertainty inherent in ML-predicted kinetic parameters. kinGEMs successfully generated ecGEMs for 93 models spanning a phylogenetically diverse set of organisms including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, mycobacteria, parasitic protists, fungi, and mammalian cell lines. These innovations breakdown the barrier to application of ecGEMs to non-model organisms and open new avenues for metabolic engineering and synthetic biology in more industrially relevant hosts.

title: Deep learning prediction of preschool language development trajectories: Multimodal modeling for early educational environments.
desc: [Early human development] Early identification of language development delays in preschool children enables timely intervention during critical developmental windows, yet existing screening tools rely on periodic snapshots that miss the dynamic, trajectory-based nature of language acquisition. This study presents a multimodal deep learning framework - a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network with multi-head attention - for predicting individual language development trajectories from birth to 24 months using acoustic, linguistic, and behavioral feature streams collected in naturalistic early educational environments. Trained on 6349 longitudinal assessments from 847 children across three collection sites, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 4.2 score points, R2 = 0.93, and an AUC-ROC of 0.94 for language delay classification. Ablation experiments confirm that multimodal fusion outperforms any single modality, with linguistic features contributing the largest marginal gain. The model accurately identifies children with language delay risk at 12 months with 84% sensitivity and 92% specificity, outperforming standard clinical screening instruments on specificity while maintaining comparable sensitivity. Subgroup analyses confirm consistent performance across socioeconomic, bilingual, and gender-based subgroups. Feature importance analysis reveals that early acoustic features dominate prediction in the first six months, while linguistic and behavioral features grow in importance across development. Practical implementation guidelines are provided for deployment in preschool and early educational settings.

title: Verifiable Agentic Science on Public Infrastructure.
source: PubMed · bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
desc: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] Autonomous artificial intelligence agents are transforming the practice of science. Across every discipline, researchers are handing data analysis to coding agents that can design and execute complex studies from a single prompt. Yet this revolution carries a threat. When agents improvise in local environments, they leave no verifiable record, ultimately risking a wave of irreproducible science. Solving this crisis requires moving agentic science onto public infrastructure where every action leaves an examinable trail. Here we connect autonomous coding agents to shared computing resources, turning ephemeral prompts into auditable scientific records. After showing that 30 unguided local agents splinter into 18 incompatible pipelines on the same dataset, we conduct an agentic reproduction and discovery study on a large scale-reproducing a large, diverse array of studies with every workflow, history, and intermediate dataset publicly accessible. This complete provenance trail exposes unstated modeling choices, reference mismatches, and subsampled tutorial inputs in published studies, and establishes a new foundation where human scientists can understand, steer, and trust AI-driven discovery.

title: Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation.
desc: [iScience] Accurate discrimination of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for early diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to lesion heterogeneity and interobserver variability in ultrasound assessment. We developed a deep learning (DL) framework integrating dual inverted bottleneck blocks (Dual-IB), adaptive hierarchical feature fusion, and knowledge distillation (KD) for breast ultrasound lesion classification. The model was trained and evaluated on public datasets and validated on an independent external cohort to assess its generalizability. Results demonstrated superior performance compared with baseline methods and resident radiologists, while maintaining robust performance across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. On the external validation dataset, the model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy (Acc) of 92.64% and an F1-score of 92.37%. Furthermore, class activation mapping (CAM) visualizations revealed focused and anatomically plausible attention patterns within lesion regions, aiding interpretation and suggesting its potential to assist in breast ultrasound lesion classification.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers' career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness.
desc: [PloS one] The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers' professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption-career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled nanomedicine development: From rational design to manufacturing optimization.
source: PubMed · Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
desc: [Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society] The translation of nanomedicines remains constrained by persistent bottlenecks, including complex design parameters, unpredictable in vivo behavior, and low diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI), with its advanced data processing and learning algorithms, offers new solutions to these challenges by learning from heterogeneous data and supporting decision-making throughout nanomedicine development. This review summarizes the AI methods and modeling workflows relevant to nanomedicine and surveys their applications in rational nanomaterial design, prediction of in vivo fate and nano-bio interactions, theranostic imaging analysis, and formulation and manufacturing optimization. This review further discusses the main barriers that currently limit translation, which largely concern data, model reliability, and computational cost. Future progress will depend on better data resources, more generalizable and interpretable models, and closer integration of AI with experimental and mechanistic approaches. We believe that through these advances, AI-enabled nanomedicine will ultimately achieve more reliable and translatable outcomes.

title: Pink noise in dyads' semantic similarity trajectories predicts conversation enjoyment.
desc: [Science advances] Conversation is a core component of human social life. Many influential theories treat conversation as a linear system, i.e., the sum of its parts. However, linear accounts of semantic entrainment lose explanatory power at their upper limits: Discussing perfectly aligned opinions becomes boring. We propose an alternate account that considers the multiscale organization of semantic similarity over the course of a conversation, as indexed by pink noise. Here, we test whether pink noise can be found in interlocutors' conavigated trajectories through semantic space. Not only is pink noise present, but its strength predicts positive conversation outcomes like enjoyment and connection, increases with practice, and is reflected in a large language model's representation of conversation quality. These results demonstrate an important role for scale-free dynamics in characterizing successful conversation.
